newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA TO LAUNCH NEW 50,000 LEI BANKNOTE.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA TO LAUNCH NEW 50,000 LEI BANKNOTE.

text.p: Romania's central bank will officially launch on Saturday its new 50,000 lei banknote, which will be put into circulation in the coming months.
Plans for the new note, which bares the face of famous 20th century composer George Enescu, have been delayed for over a year by public fears bigger banknotes mean higher inflation.
The current highest denomination note in Romania is 10,000 lei (some $3), introduced in 1994 to cope with rising printing costs and bulging wallets.

The leu is officially quoted at 3,155/65 to the dollar but private exchange houses trade it at around 3,550. Year-on-year inflation quickened to 40.3 percent in July from some 27.8 percent at end-1995.
Like many post-communist currencies the leu suffered a stunning depreciation after the bloody 1989 revolution.
In the era of Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu the leu was set at 21 to the dollar and each leu was divided into 100 bani which existed in coin form. The bani has long disappeared.
The net average wage in Romania was 333,797 lei ($105) in July. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
